dedupe_keys.name: mine water treatment schemes and coal mining monitoring points mining remediation authority

description: These two Mining Remediation Authority datasets describe how Britain manages water from abandoned coal mines. Mine water treatment schemes gives the extents of the individual schemes the Authority runs to treat water affected by past coal mining; it is published as a GeoPackage under the Open Government Licence and shown in the Authority's map viewer. Coal mining monitoring points lists sites across the UK where the Authority gathers environmental data such as water level, mine gas concentration, flow rate, chemistry and pumping data; the entry explains that as coal production and underground pumping stopped, mine water levels rose and outbreaks at the surface occurred. The monitoring points entry is served through the Scottish spatial data portal and a gov.uk publication page. The Coal Authority was renamed the Mining Remediation Authority in November 2024. Caveats: the pages read give scheme extents and point locations but not the monitoring time series themselves. For simulation it locates the pumping and treatment assets that keep mine water out of rivers and aquifers, whose failure in floods or power cuts would cause pollution, useful in water quality and interdependency models. Related catalogue records include the Environment Agency data on discharges from abandoned metal mines and the Development High Risk Area.
